basic_info.title: TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control
basic_info.affiliation: UC San Diego (consortium; not fully confirmed from abstract page)

method.notes: Performs local trajectory optimization (MPC) directly in the latent space of a learned IMPLICIT world model that has NO reconstruction decoder at all -- the model never predicts raw observations, only latent-space value/reward/dynamics. Scales to 317M-parameter multi-task agents across 80 tasks and 104 online RL tasks. This is the most direct 2023-2024 evidence for the 'reconstruction-free world model' trend: the entire class of decoder-vs-latent competition that causes Stage-2's posterior collapse (MDN GPS head + RoadScorer head both reading (h,z) and satisfying loss via h alone) cannot occur in a model with no observation-reconstruction decoder in the first place, because there is no decoder for h to freeload on.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Continuous-control robotics benchmark (locomotion, manipulation), not GPS map matching. Confirms the decoder-free world-model design pattern exists and scales, but never touches road graphs or GPS.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Same class as Think2Drive/DreamerV2/V3 -- architectural inspiration only, wrong domain; does not pre-empt the thesis's GPS map-matching application.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not directly BMW-relevant; cited as evidence for the 'remove/de-emphasize the reconstruction decoder entirely' direction as a more radical alternative to Change 13's dropout/aux-loss patches, if those prove insufficient -- Stage 2 could in principle drop or heavily de-weight the MDN GPS reconstruction head and rely on latent-space value/road prediction only, at the cost of losing direct GPS-decode interpretability.

uncertain: Whether a fully decoder-free redesign is compatible with Stage-2's evaluation protocol, which currently reports cl_gps (a reconstruction metric) as a primary gate -- removing the decoder would require redefining that gate entirely, not evaluated here.
